subject_notes: Space infrastructure rollup (Hera Systems, Made In Space, Adcole, Roccor); now also UAS via Edge Autonomy acquisition (closed June 13, 2025). Heavy SDA + AFRL contracting narrative per cohort metadata. FY2025 net loss $226.6M; total revenue $335.4M; backlog $411.2M.

claims.claim_text: Redwire is the prime mission integrator on DARPA's Otter program, leveraging the SabreSat platform to develop a revolutionary air-breathing satellite system demonstrating novel electric propulsion in Very Low Earth Orbit.
claims.subject: Redwire
claims.source_quote: Redwire is the prime mission integrator on the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency's ( DARPA ) Otter program in the U.S., which is leveraging the SabreSat platform to develop a revolutionary air-breathing satellite system and will demonstrate the use of novel electric propulsion in VLEO.

claims.claim_text: Redwire is delivering multiple advanced RF payloads for a national security satellite constellation in LEO (implied SDA/PWSA Transport or Tracking Layer participant).
claims.subject: Redwire
claims.object_value: national security LEO constellation (implied SDA Transport/Tracking Layer)
claims.source_quote: Redwire is also delivering multiple advanced RF payloads for a constellation of satellites for a national security satellite constellation in LEO.

claims.claim_text: Redwire's flight-proven space offerings have supported the Space Force GPS Satellite program, presented as core defense flight heritage.
claims.subject: Redwire
claims.object_value: Space Force GPS Satellite program / GPS III follow-on
claims.source_quote: Redwire's core space offerings are flight-proven and have supported hundreds of spacecraft, missions, and operations, including ... Space Force's GPS Satellite program.

claims.claim_text: Redwire's Defense Tech segment, anchored by the Stalker UAS (granted Authority to Operate by the Defense Innovation Unit and now on the Blue UAS List on July 14, 2025), serves U.S. Marine Corps, U.S. Army, and Five Eyes partners; the Stalker Block 40 is positioned to fill the gap between sUAS and large UAS.
claims.subject: Redwire Defense Tech (Edge Autonomy)
claims.object_value: U.S. Marine Corps, U.S. Army, Five Eyes — small UAS
claims.source_quote: The Stalker Block 30 has been proven in operations worldwide for two decades, with thousands of flight hours across six continents, meeting mission needs for customers including, but not limited to, the U.S. Marine Corps, U.S. Army, and Five Eyes partners. ... On July 14, 2025, the Stalker UAS was granted an Authority to Operate by the Defense Innovation Unit and is now on the Defense Innovation Unit Blue UAS List, enabling streamlined deployment across U.S. government agencies.

claims.claim_text: Following the Edge Autonomy acquisition (closed June 13, 2025 for $1.025B), a material portion of combined-company sales are to customers in Ukraine, and those sales have been declining and may continue to decline as the war and hostilities in Ukraine end, decline or change, or as international support for military assistance to Ukraine changes.
claims.subject: Edge Autonomy (Redwire Defense Tech)
claims.source_quote: Russia's invasion of Ukraine significantly elevated global geopolitical tensions and security concerns, and following the acquisition of Edge Autonomy, a portion of the combined company's sales are to customers in Ukraine. Those sales have been declining and may continue to decline in the event that the war and hostilities in Ukraine end, decline or change, or as a result of changes in international support for military assistance to Ukraine.

claims.claim_text: Redwire's total contracted backlog was $411.2 million as of December 31, 2025 ($299.8M Space, $111.4M Defense Tech), implying ~1.2x trailing twelve-month revenue coverage given $335.4M FY2025 revenue.
claims.subject: Redwire
claims.source_quote: As of December 31, 2025, our total contracted backlog was $411.2 million of which $299.8 million related to the Space segment and $111.4 million related to the Defense Tech segment.

claims.claim_text: Redwire performs directly or through large prime contractors for many U.S. national security agencies including DARPA, the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), U.S. Space Force, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Army, and U.S. Marine Corps.
claims.subject: Redwire
claims.object_value: DARPA / NRO / Space Force / Air Force / Army / Marine Corps
claims.source_quote: Redwire performs either directly or through large prime contractors for many U.S. national security agencies, including but not limited to, the U.S. Army, U.S. Marine Corps, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Space Force, DARPA, the National Reconnaissance Office ( NRO ), and allied national security agencies.

claims.claim_text: Redwire claims to have operationally-fielded a Link-16 compatible RF system that demonstrated the first-ever transmission of a Link-16 signal from space to ground, used by NATO members and other nations.
claims.subject: Redwire
claims.source_quote: One example of an operationally-fielded Redwire payload is a Link-16 compatible RF system which successfully demonstrated the first-ever transmission of a Link-16 signal from space to ground. Such antennas are used as part of a multi-domain network employed by the North Atlantic Treaty Organization ( NATO ) members and other nations.

claims.claim_text: Redwire's Mason program is developing critical infrastructure on the lunar surface (shielding berms, landing pads, roads, habitat foundations) in support of NASA's Artemis program; this is a NASA-funded, not DoD-J-Book, line of business (control claim).
claims.subject: Redwire
claims.source_quote: In support of NASA's Artemis program, we are also engaged in lunar research related to communications and navigation solutions as well as in-situ resource utilization. Redwire is developing Mason, which seeks to build critical infrastructure on the surface of the Moon, including shielding structures (e.g., berms), landing pads, roads, and foundations for habitats.

claims.claim_text: KPMG issued an adverse opinion on Redwire's internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025 due to material weaknesses (process-level control deployment + IT general controls); the Edge Autonomy sub (32% of consolidated revenue, 10% of total assets) was excluded from the ICFR scope. Control claim, not a J-Book claim.
claims.subject: Redwire
claims.object_value: Adverse opinion on ICFR (KPMG) + Edge Autonomy excluded from scope (32% of revenue)
claims.source_quote: management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was not effective as of December 31, 2025 because of the material weaknesses described below. ... Our independent registered public accounting firm, KPMG LLP, ... has also audited the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025, and issued an adverse opinion. ... Redwire Defense Tech Intermediate Holdings, LLC's total assets and revenues represent 10% and 32%, respectively, of the Company's consolidated total assets and total revenues.

claims.claim_text: Redwire recorded $54.5M of net unfavorable EAC adjustments in FY2025 (vs $17.7M FY2024 and $3.5M FY2023), driven by a $25.2M unfavorable adjustment including a $12.9M loss reserve on a Defense Tech program and $14.1M in Space Europe; gross margin collapsed from 15% to 5%. This is a signal that fixed-price contract performance is deteriorating.
claims.subject: Redwire
claims.object_value: $54.5M net unfavorable EAC adjustments FY2025; $12.9M Defense Tech loss reserve; $14.1M Space Europe
claims.source_quote: The net unfavorable EAC adjustments in 2025 were primarily due to a $25.2 million unfavorable adjustment, including a $12.9 million loss reserve related to a program in the Company's Defense Tech segment and $14.1 million unfavorable adjustments related to programs in the Space Europe reporting unit ... Gross profit decreased $27.2 million, or 61%, ... gross margin was 5% and 15% for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
